fig1_training_curves.title: Training dynamics and late-stage refinement.
fig1_training_curves.caption: (a) Raw and EMA validation accuracy for the three-stage reference and the four-stage model across all 400 training epochs; inset repeats the final 100 epochs at expanded scale. (b) Matched 60-epoch control and mild-appearance refinement. Curves are unsmoothed trainer BF16 evaluations without test-time augmentation, not deployment scores. Each curve is one run; late fluctuations do not establish convergence.

fig2_official_scores.title: Local, public and private rankings differ.
fig2_official_scores.caption: Scores for five unique submissions: local fixed-validation FP32 flip accuracy and screenshot-observed public/private accuracy. Outlined rows and outlined markers identify the two submissions selected for final evaluation. The selected final private score is 86.3% (robust control); the 87.3% private maximum belongs to an unselected robust-refinement submission. The duplicate screenshot row for that model is plotted once.

fig3_architecture_comparison.title: Structural variants under recorded training budgets.
fig3_architecture_comparison.caption: CPU FP32 horizontal-flip accuracy on the same 5,000 validation images (2 threads, batch 64). Labels identify selected artifacts and total branch-compute epochs, including source runs. The dotted line marks the 97.52% local champion. Budgets, channel layouts and selected artifact types differ, so the plot is descriptive rather than a causal comparison of a single architectural factor.

fig4_errors_and_robustness.title: Class-specific errors and a fixed blur proxy.
fig4_errors_and_robustness.caption: (a) Error counts with FP32 horizontal-flip inference, with 500 examples per class. (b) Original and mildly blurred accuracy without TTA on the same stratified 1,000-image subset (100 per class); blur uses a 3-by-3 Gaussian kernel with sigma 0.6. The proxy is descriptive and does not reveal hidden test labels or establish the cause of competition performance.
